classification.difficultyReason: Recognise four standard angle categories from their marked sectors.

content.prompt: Classify each angle as acute, obtuse, reflex or right.

spec.description: Rightward horizontal ray and rising rightward ray with their narrow interior angle marked; ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: The marked opening is greater than zero and less than a right angle; no numerical measure is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: No classification or numerical answer appears.

answer.worked: The marked angle is greater than $0^{\circ}$ and less than $90^{\circ}$, so it is acute.

spec.description: Rightward horizontal ray and rising leftward ray with the interior opening above the vertex marked; ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: The marked opening is greater than a right angle and less than a straight angle; no numerical measure is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: No classification or numerical answer appears.

answer.worked: The marked angle is greater than $90^{\circ}$ and less than $180^{\circ}$, so it is obtuse.

spec.description: Upward-opening V with a long exterior arc passing around the left, bottom and right of the vertex; ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: The exterior sector, rather than the smaller opening above the vertex, is selected. It exceeds a straight angle and is less than a revolution.
spec.answerVisibility: No classification or numerical answer appears.

answer.worked: The exterior arc marks an angle greater than $180^{\circ}$ and less than $360^{\circ}$, so it is reflex.

spec.description: Vertical upward and horizontal rightward rays with an interior square marker; ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular rays form the square-marked right angle.
spec.answerVisibility: The source square marker is retained; no classification text appears.

answer.worked: The square marker indicates an angle of $90^{\circ}$, so it is a right angle.
